verdict.rationale: Apple's own docs show a first-party tooling ecosystem built around Apple silicon: Xcode app building and testing across simulators, a Metal debugger for inspecting and optimizing GPU pipelines, and ML frameworks (MLX, Core ML, PyTorch Metal backends) aimed at Apple Silicon. Nothing in the pack covers compilers or CPU-level optimization guidance, so the 'mature compilers' and 'official optimization guidance' parts are thin and rest only on GPU and ML tooling. Missing for 10: evidence of compiler toolchain maturity (e.g. clang/LLVM or Swift targeting), official CPU/architecture optimization guides, third-party toolchain or OS tier-one support statements, independent developer corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, this architecture is a first-class development target — mature compilers, official optimization guidance, and an OS and tooling ecosystem that treats it as tier one

citations.quote: makes building and testing apps across multiple simulators in Xcode quicker than ever
Inspect, debug, and optimize your entire rendering pipeline with Metal debugger
MLX is an open-source array framework that lets you experiment with, training, researching, and fine-tuning generative models on Apple Silicon.
Accelerate the training of machine learning models in third-party frameworks right on your Mac with PyTorch backends.
